structures.name: Periclase
info: Mg + O both CN=6 octahedral — strongly ionic

structures.name: Cuprite
info: Copper(I) oxide phase relevant to reduction-red chemistry
Simple cubic model for redox teaching and bond topology

structures.name: Rutile
info: Ti in octahedral coordination (6 O neighbors)
Ubiquitous ceramic opacifier; also produces blue/yellow colorant effects

structures.name: Hematite
info: Iron oxide — most common ceramic colorant
Fe octahedral, red in oxidation / black in reduction

structures.name: Cassiterite
info: Tin dioxide — rutile-type structure (Sn replaces Ti)
Sn in octahedral coordination (6 O neighbors)
Traditional tin opacifier: majolica, Delft, and Bristol glazes

structures.name: Magnetite
info: Black iron oxide — reduction atmosphere product
Fe tet (8a) + Fe oct (16d): mixed valence

structures.name: Tridymite
info: Intermediate silica polymorph between quartz and cristobalite

structures.name: Forsterite
info: Mg in octahedral, Si in tetrahedral sites

structures.name: Willemite
info: Zinc orthosilicate — host mineral for crystal glazes
Large crystals grow ~900–10500°C slow-cool in oxidation

structures.name: Zircon
info: Zr-Si framework with low thermal expansion

structures.name: Diopside
info: CaMg pyroxene — mattifier & crystal glaze phase
Crystallizes Cone 9–10 reducing glazes as white crystals

structures.name: Enstatite
info: Mg octahedral + Si chain: NBO/T=2 (chain silicate)
Low-expansion pyroxene used in flameware bodies

structures.name: Spodumene
info: Chain silicate, Li in M2 cavities

structures.name: Wollastonite
info: Used in cone 6 glazes, from limestone

structures.name: Albite
info: Soda feldspar — primary flux in glazes

structures.name: Anorthite
info: Ca-feldspar — Ca end-member of plagioclase series
3D Al-Si framework, Ca in large cavities (CN=7–8)
Melts 1553°C; forms in high-Ca glaze compositions

structures.name: Nepheline
info: Framework with Na+ in hex channels

structures.name: Leucite
info: Key phase for high expansion and crazing/compression behavior

structures.name: Akermanite
info: Useful for crystalline matte pathway comparisons

structures.name: Gehlenite
info: Melilite-group phase in high-Ca/high-Al glaze systems

structures.name: Talc
info: Hydrated Mg phyllosilicate — common raw material
Mg octahedral sheet sandwiched by Si tet sheets

structures.name: Andalusite
info: Transforms toward mullite + silica during high firing

structures.name: Kyanite
info: Shows polymorph-dependent coordination and expansion behavior

structures.name: Sillimanite
info: High-temperature Al2SiO5 polymorph used in refractories

structures.name: Spinel
info: Forms at 950-1050C in alumina clay bodies

structures.name: Baddeleyite
info: Relevant for high-temperature refractory and transformation behavior

structures.name: Cubic Zirconia
info: High-symmetry zirconia phase for high-temp engineering ceramics

structures.name: Brucite
info: Mg octahedral, OH groups point out of each layer face

structures.name: Calcite
info: Calcium carbonate — most common Ca source in glazes
a=4.989 c=17.062 Angstrom (R-3c, isostructural w/ corundum)
COE=25 — extreme anisotropy causes thermal shock in body

structures.name: Dolomite
info: Calcium magnesium carbonate — ordered Ca/Mg calcite
Alternating Ca and Mg layers along c-axis; CO₃ triangles between
Decomposes in two stages: MgCO₃ → MgO+CO₂ at 760°C, CaCO₃ → CaO+CO₂ at 900°C

structures.name: Cordierite
info: Si/Al ring framework with Mg in channel-like sites

structures.name: Stabilized Zirconia
info: Track stabilizer explicitly in later schema revisions.

structures.name: Silicon Carbide
info: High thermal conductivity and strong thermal shock performance.

structures.name: Silicon Nitride
info: Useful reference material for thermal cycling and structural resilience.

structures.name: Zirconium Diboride
info: Leading-edge material for hypersonic re-entry vehicles; requires oxidation protection

structures.name: Hafnium Diboride
info: Melting point ~3380°C; higher thermal stability than ZrB₂
Density ~12.5 g/cm³; extreme material for hypersonic nose cones

structures.name: Zirconium Carbide
info: Service temperature up to 2800°C; melting point ~3540°C
High thermal conductivity (~25 W/m·K) useful for heat transfer
Lower oxidation resistance than diborides; used in internal engine components

structures.name: Hafnium Carbide
info: Extremely expensive and brittle; reserve for mission-critical surfaces
Used in rocket engine throat inserts and extreme hypersonic applications

structures.name: Tantalum Carbide
info: Often used as particle reinforcement in ultra-high-temp metal alloys
High hardness and thermal stability in extreme aerospace environments

structures.name: Yttria-Stabilized Zirconia (3 mol% Y₂O₃)
info: Tetragonal → monoclinic transformation risk on cooling
Excellent insulation (low thermal conductivity ~2 W/m·K) for gas turbine blades

structures.name: Yttria-Stabilized Zirconia (8 mol% Y₂O₃)
info: Service temperature up to 1300°C with minimal phase transition
Higher yttria content eliminates damaging tetragonal transformation

structures.name: Ceria-Stabilized Zirconia
info: Less common than YSZ; useful for redox-cycling environments
CeO₂ can undergo oxygen loss/gain affecting mechanical properties

structures.name: Hafnium Oxide
info: Service temperature up to 2000°C; superior to YSZ
Lower thermal conductivity (~1.5 W/m·K) provides better insulation
Monoclinic → tetragonal transition near 1770°C; higher refractive index

structures.name: Lanthanum Zirconate
info: Excellent phase stability; minimal thermal shock risk
Lower thermal conductivity and superior high-temp performance vs YSZ

structures.name: Ytterbium Silicate
info: Environmental barrier coating for SiC-SiC composites
Critical for protecting CMC matrices in hypersonic flight environments

structures.name: Ytterbium Disilicate
info: Tunable composition for optimizing EBC performance
Silicate structure provides excellent thermal shock resistance

structures.name: SiC-SiC Ceramic Matrix Composite
info: Service temperature up to 1300°C in next-gen engines
Low density combined with high strength and fracture toughness
Combines SiC fibers with SiC matrix; fiber coatings enable crack bridging

structures.name: Aluminum Nitride
info: Excellent thermal conductivity (~180 W/m·K) + electrical insulation
Used in thermal management and structural aerospace applications

structures.name: Boron Nitride (Hexagonal)
info: Often used as filler or lubricant additive in composites

structures.name: Sialon
info: High strength and creep resistance at temperature
Used in structural aerospace and high-speed machining applications

structures.name: Reaction-Bonded Silicon Carbide
info: Two-phase structure (SiC + residual Si); residual Si oxidizes above 1400°C

structures.name: Sintered Silicon Carbide
info: Fully dense SiC; no residual metal phase
Highest thermal properties; used in kiln shelves and thermal-structural components

structures.name: Sintered Silicon Nitride
info: Outstanding creep resistance and thermal fatigue strength
Used in advanced engine components and hypersonic vehicle structures

firingPhases.desc: Free water evaporating from clay body
Chemically bound water still in layers
Glass phase melts around mullite needles
